title: Ethereum protocol: EIP-7702 authorization chain ID mismatch
summary: An EIP-7702 authorization tuple targets a different chain ID.
likelyCauses: The authorization was signed for a different chain.
The authorization will be ignored or rejected by state transition handling.
nextSteps: Re-sign the authorization for the target chain ID.
Verify wallet chain context before sending.

title: Ethereum protocol: EIP-7702 authorization destination has code
summary: An EIP-7702 authorization points to a destination that already has contract code.
likelyCauses: The authorization destination violates EIP-7702 state transition checks.
The delegate/destination address shape is wrong for this authorization.
nextSteps: Choose a valid destination address for the authorization.
Inspect code at the destination address before signing.
examples: EIP-7702 authorization destination is a contract

title: Ethereum protocol: EIP-7702 authorization invalid signature
summary: An EIP-7702 authorization signature is invalid.
likelyCauses: The authorization tuple cannot be recovered or does not match the authority.
Wrong chain ID, nonce, delegate address, or signer can cause this.
nextSteps: Re-sign the authorization tuple with the correct authority and fields.
Verify signer domain/chain and serialized tuple.

title: Ethereum protocol: EIP-7702 authorization nonce mismatch

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)EIP-7702 authorization nonce does not match current account nonce(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: An EIP-7702 authorization nonce does not match current account state.
likelyCauses: The account nonce changed after signing or the signer used a stale nonce.
The authorization will not apply to current state.
nextSteps: Refresh the authority account nonce and re-sign.
Submit pending nonce transactions first if needed.
examples: EIP-7702 authorization nonce does not match current account nonce

title: Ethereum protocol: EIP-7702 authorization nonce overflow
summary: An EIP-7702 authorization nonce exceeds the allowed 64-bit range.
likelyCauses: The authorization nonce is outside the accepted range.
This is a signer/serialization bug.
nextSteps: Regenerate the authorization with the current account nonce.
Check nonce serialization and BigInt bounds.

title: Ethereum protocol: Blob transaction cannot create contract
summary: A blob transaction attempted contract creation without an explicit recipient.
likelyCauses: Blob transactions are not valid contract-creation transactions.
The transaction has no explicit to field.
nextSteps: Use a non-blob transaction for contract deployment.
Set an explicit recipient for blob-carrying transactions.

title: Ethereum protocol: Blob fee cap below blob base fee

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)max fee per blob gas less than block blob gas fee(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: The blob transaction maxFeePerBlobGas is below the current blob base fee.
likelyCauses: The transaction cannot pay the blob gas price required by the block.
Blob fee markets are separate from execution gas fees.
nextSteps: Refresh blob fee data and raise maxFeePerBlobGas.
Do not solve this by only changing maxFeePerGas.
examples: max fee per blob gas less than block blob gas fee

title: Ethereum protocol: KZG verification error
summary: Blob KZG commitment/proof verification failed.
likelyCauses: The blob sidecar proof does not verify against the commitment.
The blob payload, commitment, proof, or versioned hash may not match.
nextSteps: Regenerate blob commitments/proofs from the exact blob payload.
Verify sidecar and raw transaction assembly.

title: Ethereum protocol: Blob transaction missing blob hashes
summary: A blob transaction did not include required versioned blob hashes.
likelyCauses: Type-3 blob transactions must commit to blob hashes.
The raw transaction or sidecar assembly is incomplete.
nextSteps: Include versioned blob hashes and matching sidecar data.
Verify blob transaction serialization.

title: Ethereum protocol: Blob transaction has too many blobs
summary: A blob transaction exceeds the maximum blobs allowed by the active fork.
likelyCauses: The transaction includes more blobs than the protocol permits.
This is a hard validity check.
nextSteps: Reduce the number of blobs or split the data across transactions.
Check the target chain's active blob limits.
examples: blob transaction has too many blobs

title: Ethereum protocol: Transaction blob limit exceeded
summary: The transaction would exceed the blobpool's blob limit.
likelyCauses: The node will not accept this blob transaction under its current blobpool limits.
This can be a txpool policy limit even when the transaction format is otherwise valid.
nextSteps: Reduce blobs per transaction or retry when blobpool capacity frees up.
Consider sending through a node with appropriate blobpool capacity.

title: Ethereum protocol: Block already known
summary: The node already has the block being imported.
likelyCauses: The block hash is already present locally.
This usually appears during block import or peer propagation, not dapp transaction execution.
nextSteps: No action is needed unless block import is unexpectedly looping.
Check peer/import pipeline logs if repeated.

title: Ethereum protocol: Genesis not found in chain
summary: The node cannot find a genesis block for the chain database.
likelyCauses: The chain database/configuration is incomplete or points to the wrong data directory.
This is node setup, not a transaction failure.
nextSteps: Verify chain config and datadir.
Reinitialize or resync the node with the correct genesis.

title: Ethereum protocol: Block RLP size exceeds maximum
summary: A block's RLP-encoded size exceeds the active protocol/client maximum.
likelyCauses: The block is too large under active block-size validation rules.
A compliant node will reject it during import.
nextSteps: Treat the block as invalid for that chain/fork.
Check client/fork configuration if peers disagree.

title: Ethereum protocol: Contract code storage out of gas

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)contract creation code storage out of gas(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: Contract creation ran out of gas while storing runtime bytecode.
likelyCauses: The initcode completed but there was not enough gas left to pay the code-deposit cost.
Large runtime bytecode or a low deployment gas limit commonly triggers this.
nextSteps: Increase the deployment gas limit and verify runtime bytecode size.
If bytecode is near the maximum code-size limit, reduce contract size instead of only adding gas.
examples: contract creation code storage out of gas

title: Ethereum protocol: Contract address collision
summary: A contract creation attempted to deploy where code or nonce already exists.
likelyCauses: CREATE or CREATE2 resolved to an address that is already occupied.
Repeated deployments with the same deployer/salt/initcode commonly trigger this.
nextSteps: Use a new salt/deployer or avoid redeploying to an occupied address.
Check whether the target address already has code or nonce.

title: Ethereum protocol: Execution reverted
summary: The EVM executed REVERT and returned control with revert data if available.
likelyCauses: Contract logic deliberately reverted.
The revert data may contain Error(string), Panic(uint256), or a custom error selector that should be decoded next.
nextSteps: Decode the revert data and inspect the failing internal trace frame.
Changing gas only helps if the revert reason itself says gas was the precondition.

title: Ethereum protocol: Gas uint64 overflow
summary: Gas accounting overflowed the uint64 range used by the execution engine.
likelyCauses: A supplied or computed gas value exceeded the protocol/client accounting range.
This is an invalid transaction or malformed call input, not a contract revert.
nextSteps: Reduce the supplied gas value to a realistic block-bounded amount.
Check transaction construction for numeric overflow or decimal/hex mistakes.

title: Ethereum protocol: Insufficient balance for transfer
summary: The sender/account did not have enough balance for the value transfer in the current EVM call.
likelyCauses: A CALL, CREATE, or top-level transaction attempted to transfer more native ETH than the account balance allowed.
This is distinct from ERC-20 balance failures, which are contract-level reverts.
nextSteps: Check the native ETH balance of the sending account at the simulated block.
Reduce value or fund the account before retrying.

title: Ethereum protocol: Invalid code prefix 0xef
summary: Runtime bytecode begins with the reserved EOF prefix 0xef before EOF rules allow it.
likelyCauses: The contract code starts with a byte prefix reserved by the protocol.
A deployment artifact or custom bytecode generator emitted invalid runtime code.
nextSteps: Regenerate the bytecode with a supported compiler/target fork.
Inspect runtime bytecode, not just initcode.
examples: invalid code: must not begin with 0xef

title: Ethereum protocol: Invalid jump destination
summary: Execution attempted to jump to a byte offset that is not a valid JUMPDEST.
likelyCauses: The bytecode executed an invalid dynamic jump.
This can indicate corrupted calldata, wrong bytecode, compiler bug, or intentionally invalid low-level code.
nextSteps: Inspect the trace opcode location and bytecode source map.
Verify you are calling the expected contract and function selector.

title: Ethereum protocol: Invalid opcode
summary: Execution reached an opcode byte that is invalid for the active fork.
likelyCauses: The bytecode executed an undefined or disabled opcode.
Wrong bytecode, wrong chain/fork assumptions, corrupted jump targets, or deliberate INVALID can all surface this.
nextSteps: Inspect the failing program counter and opcode.
Verify contract bytecode and compiler target for the chain/fork being simulated.

title: Ethereum protocol: Max call depth exceeded
summary: EVM call depth exceeded the protocol limit.
likelyCauses: The call stack reached the EVM maximum depth.
Deep recursive calls or proxy/callback loops can trigger this exceptional halt.
nextSteps: Inspect the internal call trace for recursion or callback loops.
Change call structure; more gas will not increase the call-depth limit.

title: Ethereum protocol: Max code size exceeded
summary: Contract creation produced runtime bytecode above the protocol code-size limit.
likelyCauses: The deployed runtime bytecode is larger than the active maximum code size.
Adding gas cannot bypass the code-size rule.
nextSteps: Reduce runtime bytecode size, split modules, or use libraries/proxies intentionally.
Check compiler settings and metadata size.

title: Ethereum protocol: Max initcode size exceeded
summary: Contract creation initcode exceeded the protocol initcode-size limit.
likelyCauses: The creation bytecode is too large for the active fork rules.
This is usually a deployment artifact issue, not a fee issue.
nextSteps: Reduce constructor/initcode size or move initialization out of deployment.
Check EIP-3860-era initcode limits for the target chain.

title: Ethereum protocol: Nonce uint64 overflow
summary: EVM account nonce overflowed its allowed integer range.
likelyCauses: A create/transaction path would increment an account nonce beyond the protocol/client limit.
This is a hard validity problem, not a transient mempool issue.
nextSteps: Use a different account/address path.
Do not retry unchanged; the nonce range cannot be raised with gas.

title: Ethereum protocol: Out of gas
summary: Execution consumed all gas supplied to the current call frame.
likelyCauses: The call frame did not have enough gas to complete execution.
This can be caused by an underestimated gas limit, expensive calldata/storage work, or a loop/path that is more expensive than expected.
nextSteps: Estimate gas against the same state and calldata.
If the call is otherwise valid, raise the transaction gas limit; do not confuse this with raising maxFeePerGas.

title: Ethereum protocol: Return data out of bounds
summary: Bytecode attempted to copy return data outside the available returndata buffer.
likelyCauses: RETURNDATACOPY used an offset/length beyond the last call's returndata size.
This is usually a low-level assembly or proxy decoding bug.
nextSteps: Inspect the failing opcode and previous call return length.
Fix the low-level return-data copy bounds.

title: Ethereum protocol: Stack overflow
summary: Execution attempted to exceed the EVM stack limit.
likelyCauses: The EVM stack exceeded its maximum size.
This usually comes from invalid bytecode or pathological assembly/control flow.
nextSteps: Inspect the trace around the failing opcode.
Fix bytecode/control flow; more transaction gas will not increase stack depth.

title: Ethereum protocol: Stack underflow
summary: An opcode required more stack items than were available.
likelyCauses: The bytecode executed an opcode without enough stack operands.
This usually indicates invalid bytecode, a bad jump target, or low-level assembly/compiler output gone wrong.
nextSteps: Inspect the opcode trace at the failing program counter.
Verify bytecode/source-map alignment and dynamic jump paths.

title: Ethereum protocol: Write protection in static context
summary: A STATICCALL context attempted to modify state.
likelyCauses: A view/static call path tried to execute SSTORE, LOG, CREATE, SELFDESTRUCT, or another state-changing operation.
This commonly happens when a supposedly read-only function reaches mutating code through an internal call.
nextSteps: Check whether the call was made through eth_call/static context.
Move state changes out of the static path or send a real transaction.

title: Ethereum RPC block hash not found
summary: The requested block hash/number is not available to the node.
likelyCauses: The block identifier does not exist in the node's current canonical or retained state.
EIP-1474 recommends Resource not found for missing block identifiers.
nextSteps: Check the block hash/number and chain.
Use an archive node if the request depends on historical state.

title: Ethereum RPC block is not canonical
summary: A blockHash request with canonicality requirements resolved to a non-canonical block.
likelyCauses: The block exists but is not in the canonical chain according to the node.
EIP-1474 recommends distinguishing this from block-not-found.
nextSteps: Retry with the canonical block hash/number.
If querying reorged data, use a node/archive source that preserves it.

title: Ethereum RPC quantity is empty
summary: EIP-1474 quantities must not be the empty hex string.
likelyCauses: A JSON-RPC quantity was sent as 0x or empty instead of a canonical hex quantity.
Zero must be encoded as 0x0.
nextSteps: Encode zero as 0x0 and other quantities with no leading zeroes.
Validate RPC parameter serialization before sending.

title: Ethereum RPC quantity has leading zeroes
summary: EIP-1474 quantities must use the fewest possible hex digits.
likelyCauses: A numeric RPC parameter was encoded with leading zeroes.
Examples like 0x00 or 0x0400 are invalid quantities.
nextSteps: Normalize quantities to minimal 0x-prefixed hex.
Do not left-pad numeric quantity fields.
examples: hex number with leading zero digits

title: Ethereum RPC quantity missing 0x prefix
summary: EIP-1474 quantities and data values must be 0x-prefixed.
likelyCauses: A JSON-RPC parameter omitted the required 0x prefix.
Clients reject non-canonical Ethereum hex values.
nextSteps: Prefix hex quantities/data with 0x.
Use a JSON-RPC serializer that distinguishes quantity and data encodings.

title: Ethereum protocol: EIP-7702 cannot create contract

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)EIP-7702 transaction cannot be used to create contract(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: An EIP-7702 set-code transaction attempted contract creation.
likelyCauses: Set-code transactions cannot use the contract-creation path.
The transaction has no normal recipient where one is required.
nextSteps: Use a contract-creation transaction for deployment.
Use EIP-7702 set-code only with the supported recipient/authorization shape.
examples: EIP-7702 transaction cannot be used to create contract

title: Ethereum protocol: EIP-7702 empty auth list
summary: An EIP-7702 set-code transaction has no authorization tuples.
likelyCauses: Set-code transactions require at least one authorization.
The transaction is invalid before execution.
nextSteps: Attach a valid authorization list or use a different transaction type.
Verify wallet/signer support for EIP-7702.
examples: EIP-7702 transaction with empty auth list

title: Ethereum protocol: Max fee exceeds uint256
summary: The max fee cap exceeds the maximum uint256 value.
likelyCauses: The maxFeePerGas field is numerically impossible.
This is a transaction-construction bug.
nextSteps: Fix fee cap serialization and units.
Use a sane maxFeePerGas value.
examples: max fee per gas higher than 2^256-1

title: Ethereum protocol: Max fee below base fee

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)max fee per gas less than block base fee(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: The transaction max fee cap is below the block base fee.
likelyCauses: The transaction cannot pay the current base fee.
The fee cap may have been stale by the time it reached the node.
nextSteps: Refresh fee data and set maxFeePerGas above current base fee plus intended tip.
Retrying can help only after changing fee caps or when base fee drops.
examples: max fee per gas less than block base fee
fee cap less than base fee

title: Ethereum protocol: Gas limit overflow
summary: Transaction gas accounting overflowed the allowed gas-limit range.
likelyCauses: The gas limit or remaining gas pool exceeded uint64 accounting bounds.
This usually means malformed transaction construction.
nextSteps: Use a realistic gas limit below the block gas limit.
Check decimal/hex unit conversion in the transaction builder.

title: Ethereum protocol: Gas limit reached
summary: The transaction needs more gas than remains available in the block gas pool.
likelyCauses: The transaction gas limit cannot fit in the current block gas allowance.
This can appear during block processing or local inclusion checks.
nextSteps: Lower the transaction gas limit if possible or wait for a block with enough available gas.
If the transaction genuinely needs more than the block limit, it cannot be included as-is.

title: Ethereum protocol: Transaction gas limit too high
summary: The transaction gas limit exceeds the protocol/client maximum for a single transaction.
likelyCauses: The supplied transaction gas limit is above the active per-transaction cap.
This is a validity check, not an execution revert.
nextSteps: Reduce the gas limit below the active chain cap.
If execution needs more than the cap, split the operation.

title: Ethereum protocol: Insufficient gas for floor data gas cost

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)insufficient gas for floor data gas cost(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: The transaction gas limit is below the calldata floor cost required by active fork rules.
likelyCauses: Protocol calldata floor pricing requires more gas than supplied.
Execution did not start.
nextSteps: Raise gas limit to cover floor data gas.
Check calldata size and active fork rules.
examples: insufficient gas for floor data gas cost

title: Ethereum protocol: Insufficient funds for gas * price + value
summary: The sender cannot cover maximum gas cost plus transferred value.
likelyCauses: Native balance is below value plus the transaction's maximum fee exposure.
For EIP-1559 transactions, maxFeePerGas and gas limit determine the up-front affordability check.
nextSteps: Fund the sender, lower value, lower gas limit, or lower fee caps where safe.
Remember this is native ETH balance, not ERC-20 balance.
examples: insufficient funds for gas * price + value

title: Ethereum protocol: Insufficient funds for transfer
summary: The sender lacks enough native ETH for the transaction value transfer.
likelyCauses: The transaction value exceeds the sender's available native balance before execution costs.
This is a top-level transaction precheck.
nextSteps: Fund the sender or lower the transaction value.
Also account for gas fees separately.

title: Ethereum protocol: Insufficient funds for witness access costs

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)insufficient funds to cover witness access costs for transaction(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: The sender cannot cover protocol witness access or modification costs.
likelyCauses: The transaction passed basic value checks but cannot cover witness-related execution costs.
This is a protocol cost-accounting failure, not a contract revert.
nextSteps: Fund the sender with additional native ETH.
Review the target fork's witness/access-cost rules.
examples: insufficient funds to cover witness access costs for transaction

title: Ethereum protocol: Intrinsic gas too low
summary: The supplied gas limit is below the transaction's intrinsic gas cost.
likelyCauses: Base transaction cost, calldata bytes, access list, blob/auth data, or creation overhead exceed the gas limit.
Execution did not start.
nextSteps: Let the client estimate gas, or compute intrinsic gas for calldata/access/blob/auth fields.
Raise the gas limit above intrinsic cost.

title: Ethereum protocol: Invalid transaction v, r, s values
summary: The transaction signature fields are invalid.
likelyCauses: The transaction signature is malformed or not valid under Ethereum signature rules.
Bad chain ID/signing mode or corrupted raw transaction bytes can trigger this.
nextSteps: Re-sign the transaction with the correct chain ID and transaction type.
Verify raw transaction serialization.
examples: invalid transaction v, r, s values

title: Ethereum protocol: Nonce has max value
summary: The sender nonce is already at the maximum representable value.
likelyCauses: The account nonce cannot be incremented further under protocol/client limits.
The transaction is invalid for that sender.
nextSteps: Use a different sender account.
Do not retry unchanged; gas and fees cannot fix nonce exhaustion.

title: Ethereum protocol: Nonce too high
summary: The transaction nonce is above the next nonce expected by current state.
likelyCauses: One or more earlier nonce transactions are missing or pending.
Nodes may hold or reject the transaction depending on txpool policy.
nextSteps: Submit or confirm the missing lower nonce transactions first.
Check pending pool state for the sender.

title: Ethereum protocol: Nonce too low
summary: The transaction nonce is below the sender account nonce in state.
likelyCauses: The account has already used this nonce on-chain or in the node's pending view.
The transaction is stale unless it is replacing a pending transaction with the same nonce and acceptable fees.
nextSteps: Refresh the account nonce from the target chain.
Submit the next nonce, or intentionally replace the pending transaction with a sufficient fee bump.

title: Ethereum protocol: Sender not an EOA
summary: The transaction sender is a contract account where an EOA sender is required.
likelyCauses: Protocol rules reject transactions whose sender account has code.
This commonly indicates a wrong from address or account-abstraction flow sent as a normal transaction.
nextSteps: Use an EOA as the transaction sender.
For smart accounts, send through the correct account-abstraction or contract entry point.

title: Ethereum protocol: Priority fee above max fee

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)max priority fee per gas higher than max fee per gas(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: The priority fee cap is greater than the total max fee cap.
likelyCauses: EIP-1559 requires maxPriorityFeePerGas <= maxFeePerGas.
The transaction is invalid before execution.
nextSteps: Set maxFeePerGas at least as high as maxPriorityFeePerGas.
Recalculate fee caps from the same unit system.
examples: max priority fee per gas higher than max fee per gas

title: Ethereum protocol: Priority fee exceeds uint256

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)max priority fee per gas higher than 2\^256-1(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: The priority fee cap exceeds the maximum uint256 value.
likelyCauses: The priority fee field is numerically impossible.
This is a transaction-construction bug.
nextSteps: Fix fee cap serialization and units.
Use a sane maxPriorityFeePerGas value.
examples: max priority fee per gas higher than 2^256-1

title: Ethereum protocol: Transaction type not supported

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)transaction type does not supported eip-155 protected signatures(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: The transaction type is not valid for the active network/fork or signature mode.
likelyCauses: The node does not accept this typed transaction under current chain configuration.
This can happen when sending dynamic-fee/blob/set-code transactions to a chain or fork that has not enabled them.
nextSteps: Use a transaction type supported by the target chain.
Verify chain ID, hardfork, and signer settings.
examples: transaction type does not supported eip-155 protected signatures

title: Ethereum protocol: Transaction uint256 overflow
summary: A transaction numeric field is too large for uint256.
likelyCauses: A value, gas, fee, nonce, chain ID, or other numeric input exceeded uint256 bounds.
This is usually a transaction builder/unit conversion bug.
nextSteps: Clamp numeric fields to valid uint256 values.
Check decimal string, hex quantity, and BigInt conversions.
examples: bigint overflow, too large for uint256

title: Ethereum protocol: Account limit exceeded
summary: The sender has too many transactions in the node's txpool.
likelyCauses: The pool enforces a per-account queued/pending transaction limit.
Additional transactions from that sender are rejected until earlier ones clear.
nextSteps: Wait for pending transactions to confirm/drop or use fewer queued nonces.
Avoid bulk-sending many transactions from one account.

title: Ethereum protocol: Address already reserved
summary: The sender already has a transaction reserved in another txpool subpool.
likelyCauses: A blob and non-blob transaction from the same sender can conflict across subpools.
The node avoids mixing incompatible pending transaction classes for the account.
nextSteps: Wait for or replace the existing reserved transaction.
Submit transactions for the sender in a consistent blob/non-blob sequence.

title: Ethereum protocol: Already known
summary: The transaction is already known by the node's transaction pool.
likelyCauses: The same transaction hash is already pending or queued.
Rebroadcasting identical raw bytes is redundant.
nextSteps: Check whether the transaction hash is already pending.
Only resend if using a different node or if propagation failed.

title: Ethereum protocol: Exceeds block gas limit
summary: The transaction gas limit exceeds the current block gas limit.
likelyCauses: No block can include the transaction with that gas limit under current rules.
Execution has not started.
nextSteps: Reduce the gas limit below the block limit.
If the operation genuinely needs more gas than the block allows, split it.

title: Ethereum protocol: Transaction gas price below minimum
summary: The transaction is below the txpool's configured minimum gas price.
likelyCauses: The node refuses to admit transactions under its minimum gas price threshold.
This is a local policy error, not a consensus execution failure.
nextSteps: Raise fee caps/gas price or use a node with a lower minimum.
Do not change calldata or gas limit unless those are also wrong.

title: Ethereum protocol: In-flight delegated transaction limit reached

patterns.value: (?:^|.*\b)in-flight transaction limit reached for delegated accounts(?:\b|:|$).*

summary: The node reached its in-flight transaction limit for delegated accounts.
likelyCauses: EIP-7702 delegated-account txpool policy limits are exhausted.
This is a mempool admission limit, not a contract revert.
nextSteps: Wait for in-flight delegated transactions to clear.
Throttle submissions for delegated accounts.
examples: in-flight transaction limit reached for delegated accounts

title: Ethereum protocol: Invalid sender
summary: The transaction sender cannot be recovered or is not valid.
likelyCauses: The signature, chain ID, or transaction encoding does not recover a valid sender.
This is a transaction construction/signing failure.
nextSteps: Re-sign with the correct chain ID and transaction type.
Verify raw transaction serialization before broadcasting.

title: Ethereum protocol: Negative transaction value
summary: The transaction value field is negative or decoded as negative.
likelyCauses: Ethereum transaction values must be non-negative unsigned integers.
This is a serialization or transaction-construction bug.
nextSteps: Fix value serialization and units.
Use unsigned integer transaction value fields only.

title: Ethereum protocol: Oversized transaction data
summary: The transaction calldata exceeds a node txpool anti-DoS size policy.
likelyCauses: The input data is too large for the node's transaction pool policy.
This may be policy-level rather than consensus-level, but execution has not started.
nextSteps: Reduce calldata size or split the operation.
Try a node with compatible txpool limits only if the transaction is otherwise valid.

title: Ethereum protocol: Replacement transaction underpriced
summary: A same-nonce replacement did not increase fees enough.
likelyCauses: The node already has a pending transaction from this sender with the same nonce.
The replacement must satisfy the pool's configured price-bump rule.
nextSteps: Increase maxFeePerGas and maxPriorityFeePerGas enough to meet replacement rules.
Or wait for/drop the existing pending transaction before resubmitting.

title: Ethereum protocol: Transaction underpriced
summary: The transaction fee is below the node's minimum txpool acceptance price.
likelyCauses: The node considers the gas price or fee cap too low for mempool admission.
This is txpool policy; execution has not started.
nextSteps: Refresh fee data and raise the relevant fee cap/tip.
Retrying unchanged is unlikely to help on the same node.
